title: Policy-driven audit egress router and customer-blob lifecycle for VPC/on-prem
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Private and VPC customers need an audit egress path that can: (1) enforce routing & retention policies per-tenant, (2) forward immutable audit bundles to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Azure) while supporting CMEK/HSM and resumable uploads, and (3) be operable in on-prem and airgapped installs. This ticket scopes the design and implementation of a policy-driven egress router (audit egress router) and the customer-blob lifecycle guarantees for private/VPC/on-prem deployments.

Goals:
- Define policy model enabling admins and RBAC v2 roles to control where audit logs may be forwarded and what transformations are allowed (e.g., redaction, partitioning).
- Provide a pluggable forwarder with adapters for S3/GCS/Azure and an SFTP/HTTPS sink for on-prem scenarios.
- Ensure customer-managed encryption key support (CMEK/HSM) and signed resumable uploads with integrity proofs.
- Preserve SAML/SSO context and admin auditing in forwarded records to support forensics.
- Create rollout path for Dedicated and Private deployments with a gradual opt-in and migration for existing audit-shipper users.

Non-goals:
- Full UI for Console; initial phase exposes APIs and config templates, Console work will be follow-up (PM ticket).

Constraints and assumptions:
- Network egress from Private installs may be restricted; must support operator-controlled connectors that run inside customer VPC and push to their buckets.
- On-prem customers may prefer pull-based collectors; design includes optional pull adapter but primary will be push with resumable multipart uploads.
- Retention enforcement is cooperative: the forwarder must annotate retention intent and provide deletion hooks for customer side; we cannot delete customer-managed objects automatically without explicit operator workflow.

High-level design decisions:
1) Policy model: YAML/JSON policy attached to tenant configuration. Policies express allowed sinks (url patterns), retention class (short|standard|archive), mandatory labels to attach, and transformations (none|redact-PII|truncate-contents). Policies are enforceable by RBAC v2 roles; only users with audit_admin or infra_admin may modify forwarder policies.

2) Forwarder architecture: lightweight forwarder process running in control plane for Hosted, and as an operator/controller for Private/VPC. It accepts signed audit bundles, performs deterministic transformations, and queues multipart resumable uploads to customer sinks. Forwarder will maintain local encrypted queue with sequence numbers and a signed manifest for provenance.

3) Adapters: S3/GCS/Azure adapters will support server-side encryption (customer-provided keys where applicable) and SSE-C variants. On-prem adapter supports SFTP and HTTPS with mutual TLS. All adapters emit an upload receipt (signed) that we store in tenant metadata for later verification.

4) CMEK/HSM: Expose metadata for the customer to provide KMS key identifiers and handshake tokens. For hosted-managed uploads to customer buckets, we will support KMS-encrypted objects by performing client-side encryption with keys provided via a secure handshake (never persisting plaintext keys). For Private, operators may inject key access via vault integrations.

5) SAML/SSO linkage: Audit entries forwarded must preserve SAML principal attributes (if present) and include an assertion_id reference. The forwarder will map internal subject IDs to SAML principals at export time and include a signed linkage artifact.

6) Observability & integrity: Each forwarded object will include a manifest JSON: {sequence, tenant, policy_id, transform, sha256, signed_by}. The manifest is included as object metadata and also posted to the control plane index. This enables replay verification and efficient regression detection in Redwood Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy CRUD API implemented and RBAC v2 enforcement wired to audit_admin role (manual tests pass).
- Forwarder operator container built and validated in staging with S3 and SFTP adapters.
- Multipart resumable uploads validated for large (100GB) bundles with checkpoint/resume after simulated interruption.
- Signed upload receipts and manifests generated and verifiable using public key of forwarder.
- Security review completed and design doc updated with threat mitigations.

Rollout plan:
1. Implementation and unit/integration tests (this ticket).
2. Staging deployment with test tenant and customer-mock buckets (QA week).
3. Canary in-hosted for low-volume tenants with opt-in flag (2 weeks).
4. Private/VPC operator delivery as an image and Helm chart + operator-docs (release).
5. Migrate existing shipper users via opt-in migration tool that replays recent audit bundles and stitches manifests.

Compliance notes:
- Logs must be tamper-evident; manifests and signed receipts are mandatory for compliance customers.
- Provide a path to generate CA-signed material for on-prem mutual TLS and confirm certificate rotation story.

Remaining open questions:
- Do we enforce retention deletion via operator workflows for Private installs, or provide deletion playbooks only? (Security asks for stronger guarantees.)
- How to negotiate KMS access for cross-account GCS/Azure uploads without revealing key material? (We propose one-time envelope key exchange.)

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Egress+Router+Design (private)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/182 (WIP)
